subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should valid ignore files that are below the byte cap but exceed new pattern-count or pattern-length limits be treated as unreadable and hide their entire workspace subtree?
rationale: This is a new compatibility and availability contract for existing workspaces, not a mechanical consequence of bounding reads; it can make previously discoverable skills and files disappear without a configuration or migration path.

options.title: Preserve valid under-cap policies
options.body: Keep the byte cap for memory safety, but parse valid files below that cap without the new terminal complexity denial path.

options.title: Adopt terminal complexity limits
options.body: Approve the additional fail-closed policy, document the affected valid inputs, and require exact-head proof that its workspace-discovery tradeoff is intentional.

recommendation.title: Preserve valid under-cap policies
recommendation.body: Keep the byte cap for memory safety, but parse valid files below that cap without the new terminal complexity denial path.
